Title: Anti-illegal racing op on Linkedua nets 75 summonses, 31 motorcycles
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI: Police issued 75 summonses and seized 31 motorcycles in an operation at the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link (Linkedua) early this morning after identifying illegal racing hotspots where motorcyclists would perform dangerous stunts and disturb public order.
Acting district police chief superintendent Saifullah Jaya @ Yahaya said 50 motorcyclists and pillon riders - 48 men and two women, along with 42 motorcycles were checked during the operation from 1am to 4am.
"Offences found included not having side mirrors, no registration plates, fancy registration plates that do not follow specifications, modifying the vehicle structure such as exhaust pipes, not having driving licence and insurance coverage.
"A total of 31 motorcycles were seized," he said in a statement today, adding that 75 summonses were issued for violations of the Road Transport Act 1987.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tesla to launch Cybercab robotaxi in Texas early September
Article:
SAN FRANCISCO: US electric vehicle maker Tesla will launch its Cybercab robotaxi early September, reported Xinhua quoting a Tesla-focused news outlet Teslarati report.
The launch is scheduled for Sept 3 in Austin, Texas, where the company is headquartered, said Teslarati, which received an invitation to the event.
Tesla has not publicly confirmed the date.
Industry observers said the event is expected to focus not only on unveiling a new vehicle but also on introducing a purpose-built autonomous vehicle.
The Cybercab is designed without a steering wheel or pedals and relies entirely on self-driving software for near-full autonomy.
Tesla CEO Elon Musk has previously said the company plans to sell the Cybercab to private customers for less than US$30,000 apiece.
First unveiled in October 2024, the Cybercab is central to Tesla's robotaxi ambitions. It is expected to operate alongside Model Y vehicles, which have been used for autonomous passenger rides in real-world conditions for more than a year.
According to tech publication The Information, Tesla plans to initially deploy Cybercab vehicles by offering rides to employees on public roads before integrating them into its commercial robotaxi service.
The launch would mark another step in Tesla's push into autonomous driving, with robotaxi services expected to play a key role in the company's future revenue model and artificial intelligence strategy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Employer charged with harbouring 127 undocumented migrants
Article:
PASIR MAS: A Malaysian employer was charged at the Sessions Court today with allowing 127 undocumented migrants to remain at a premises under his control in Sering, Kota Baru, on Aug 10.
Nasrullah Abdullah, 43, pleaded not guilty to the charge and claimed trial before Judge Zulkpli Abdullah.
Nasrullah, from Jerteh, Terengganu, was charged under Section 55E(1) of the Immigration Act 1959/63.
He was alleged to have committed the offence at a proposed People's Housing Project construction site in Sering, Kota Baru, at about 3pm on Aug 10.
The charge stated that the 127 undocumented migrants had allegedly committed offences under Section 6(1)(c) and Section 15(1)(c) of the Immigration Act 1959/63 and Regulation 39(b) of the Immigration Regulations 1963.
If convicted under Section 55E(2) of the Immigration Act, an offender is liable to a fine of between RM5,000 and RM30,000, or jail term of up to 12 months, or both, for each undocumented migrant found on the premises.
For a second or subsequent conviction, the offender faces a fine of between RM10,000 and RM60,000, or jail of up to two years, or both, for each undocumented migrant found on the premises.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Abu Arsalnaa Zainal Abidin offered bail at RM20,000 with one surety.
However, lawyer Amy Zairy Rahmat, representing Nasrullah, urged the court to reduce the bail to not more than RM10,000.
She said her client had cooperated with the Immigration Department from the beginning and had appeared in court today, which showed his sense of responsibility.
"The proposed bail of RM20,000 is too high. We hope the court will reduce it to not more than RM10,000," she said.
The judge allowed bail at RM10,000 with one surety.
The court fixed Sept 20 for the prosecution to hand over the relevant documents.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BN should stand on its own without treating rivals as enemies – Perak MCA
Article:
IPOH: Barisan Nasional must be prepared to face the upcoming general election on its own without treating other political coalitions as enemies, says Perak MCA.
Perak MCA chairman Datuk Dr Mah Hang Soon said voters must not be left confused about the values BN represents.
Instead, BN must serve as the primary platform for citizens seeking progress without extremism, reform without chaos, and the protection of rights without sacrificing national unity.
Mah, who is also MCA deputy president, said the greatest challenge in today's political landscape lies in navigating political cooperation and competition amidst an uncertain, fragile, and suspicious environment.
"Cooperation may happen depending on the circumstances, but it must not obscure our identity, principles, and responsibilities to the voters. BN has proven itself as a big family that accommodates and unites all races in Malaysia.
"BN must maintain consistent, transparent, and explainable principles. The people have a right to know what stands we are fighting for, what we can do for stability, and what we will not sacrifice," he said.
He said this to reporters after attending the Perak MCA 16th General Election (GE16) Training Camp at MH Hotel here today. Also present were Perak BN chairman and Perak Chief Minister Datuk Seri Saarani Mohamad and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong.
Mah said an essential principle moving forward is to win back voters rather than turn them away through anger, noting that some former BN supporters had shifted their support elsewhere.
He added that these voters should not be labelled or insulted, as they may simply be disappointed, keen to explore other options, or unclear about BN's offerings.
"Our job is to listen, address our weaknesses, provide service, and convince them that BN and MCA have learned and are ready to work better.
"We must win their hearts before we win their votes. In many constituencies, the margin between victory and defeat could be just a few hundred votes," he said.
"A single family convinced, a single trader assisted, or a single local issue resolved can bring about a major shift and turn the tide toward victory," he added.
On the training camp, Mah said the initiative must serve as a turning point to rectify weaknesses and consolidate strengths.
He said MCA must integrate its core strengths, including aligning overarching narratives, managing operations rooms, and coordinating cross-ethnic mobilisation.
"We must also be honest about our organisational shortcomings, as some branches are strong while others require reinforcement. Some areas possess good voter data, while others still rely on assumptions.
"MCA needs to step up efforts to listen to community problems, serve the people, strengthen ties with residents' associations and traders, and deepen engagement with urban youths and young families," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: FT Pas sets up 11 task forces for GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Federal territories Pas will establish 11 specialised task forces - one for each of its policy offerings under its "Wilayah Sejahtera" vision - to develop concrete policies ahead of the 16th general election.
FT Pas commissioner Azhar Yahya said the task forces, announced at the Federal Territories Pas Convention here today, would each comprise experts, professionals and technocrats relevant to their respective areas.
"We are ready not merely in body, not merely in attire, but ready in terms of what we want to bring; what content we want to put forward," he said.
He said the convention, held ahead of Pas Muktamar in September, adopted 12 resolutions under the Wilayah Sejahtera theme, with the 12th resolution being the formal commitment to establish the task forces.
The resolutions covered housing affordability, public transport, cost-of-living relief, and plans to make the Federal Territories a hub for jobs and entrepreneurship for local residents.
Other resolutions addressed digital transformation, flood control and green spaces, the strengthening of Islamic institutions and inter-religious harmony, education and skills training, and better healthcare access for the elderly, disabled and low-income groups.
Pas also called for integrity and transparency in Federal Territories governance, and a comprehensive development plan for Labuan covering water, housing, tourism and the digital economy.
Azhar highlighted that the task forces were designed to showcase Pas' technocratic depth.
"People say we only have religious scholars. No. We have many technocrats, and those technocrats will now be highlighted in these task forces.
"They, not me as a religious figure, will be the ones developing the detailed policies."
Azhar said the convention served as a preparatory exercise for all Pas divisions in the Federal Territories to internalise the Wilayah Sejahtera vision, with each division tasked with bringing the discussions back to the grassroots level.
"We are waiting for the war whistle to be blown, the war drums to be beaten.
"When that happens, we will begin offering a manifesto built from the ground up, from the branches and divisions," he said.
Deputy commissioner II and head of the Federal Territories Pas Strategic Studies Institute (IPSP) Dr Ahmad Nadzri Mansor said the offerings were drawn from proposals brought by representatives from 15 divisions and councils, supplemented by feedback gathered through an 80,000-engagement social media survey.
"All the people's issues are already in our hands. We have feedback from the public, and from that we put forward the resolutions," Ahmad said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'I had only them in this world': Daughter mourns father, sisters killed in Immigration truck crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Let's eat. Let's go to the night market. I'll buy you something."
Those simple invitations from her father and two younger sisters are now painful memories for Siti Shakira, who lost all three when an Immigration Department truck ploughed into them at an intersection on Jalan Sultan Ismail here last Wednesday.
In a Facebook post yesterday, Shakira, the eldest daughter of Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaikh Yahya, said she was still struggling to come to terms with the sudden loss, which came a day before her birthday.
"Ya Allah, I cannot cope with all this, but I am trying to stay strong. I am staying strong for my mother.
"This is such a huge test for me. A day before my birthday, I was tested with the sudden loss of my father and both my sisters," she wrote.
Shakira said she still found it difficult to believe that her father and sisters were gone, adding that their family of five had now been reduced to just her and her mother.
She said she would miss the memories they shared and the familiar words from her father and sisters.
Her father would often ask, "Along, let's eat", while her sister Siti Norshazlin would invite her to the night market and her youngest sister, Siti Darwisyah Auni, would ask her to buy her something.
"All these words are still ringing in my head," she wrote.
Shakira said she had always relied on her father, who remained by her side even after she got married.
"I had only them in this world. Whenever I went anywhere, I went with them.
"My father never left me even though he knew I was already married. This is such a difficult test for me, Ya Allah," she wrote.
She said she would remain strong for her mother, who was also injured in the crash, and hoped she would recover soon.
"Please recite Al-Fatihah for them and pray that my mother recovers quickly. I am trying to stay strong and accept all that has been destined for me," she wrote.
Shakira also expressed gratitude for the public's support and prayers, saying she was comforted by the positive things people had shared about her father and sisters.
"I am grateful that I have only read good things about them. I did not realise they were so loved. I am happy that so many people are praying for them and love them."
The crash occurred when the Immigration Department lorry allegedly entered the Jalan Sultan Ismail intersection when the traffic light was red, despite its beacon lights and siren being activated.
A Proton Saga travelling through the intersection on a green light then collided with the lorry.
The impact caused the lorry to skid and
hit four pedestrians and an Inokom Matrix,
killing Shaik Mohd Firdaus Shaik Yahya, 53, and his two daughters, Siti Norshazlin, 25, and Siti Darwisyah Auni, 12.
Shaik's wife, Norhayati, was injured in the crash, suffering injuries to her head, hands and both legs.
On Thursday, the lorry driver, Mohd Akbar Zainol, was charged in the Kuala Lumpur magistrate's court with five offences.
These included three charges under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 for causing the deaths of the three family members, and one charge under Section 43(1) of the same Act for reckless and inconsiderate driving resulting in injuries to Norhayati.
He pleaded not guilty to all charges and was granted bail of RM60,000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: VIP escorts must not come at the expense of road safety
Article:
LETTERS:
Sharanjit Singh's report in the New Sunday Times, titled 'Sirens On, Rules Off?' rightly draws attention to a serious and growing concern: VIP escorts and certain emergency vehicles often move on our roads in ways that put ordinary drivers at unnecessary risk.
Most of us have experienced this.
Sirens and flashing lights come suddenly from behind, with little warning.
Drivers have to brake hard, swerve into crowded lanes, or slow down fast — often with barely enough time to react safely.
For many motorists, this is not just inconvenient; it is genuinely frightening.
Some feel nervous every time they hear a siren.
Worse, there have been reports of accidents caused directly by these sudden, unannounced moves.
It is even more worrying when sirens and beacon lights are treated not as urgent warnings, but as a free pass.
Some vehicles seem to think that with a siren, speed limits do not matter and red lights need not be obeyed.
They expect every other road user to get out of the way instantly, without thinking about road conditions or other people's safety. These are safety tools, not symbols of status.
This is why we need a full review of the rules. We need systems that give drivers enough time to move over safely, instead of demanding instant, panic-driven reactions.
Where escorts are needed, traffic police should be at junctions to guide traffic and keep things safe.
We also need clear rules on who actually gets an escort. Most people agree that only the prime minister, royalty, and official foreign guests should have them as a normal practice.
For others, including ministers and senior officials, such arrangements should be rare exceptions, not something they expect as a right.
No one is above the law. A siren does not cancel traffic rules, and a flashing light does not make safety less important.
Every road user, no matter their rank, deserves to travel safely — and every road user must drive with care.
TAN SRI LEE LAM THYE
KUALA LUMPUR

Title: 51 incidents reported in southern Thailand including IED attacks
Article:
RANTAU PANJANG: A total of 51 incidents, including attacks involving improvised explosive devices (IEDs), were reported across Thailand's three southern border provinces last night.
According to an update issued by the Internal Security Operations Command Region 4 (ISOC 4), the incidents were reported in 12 areas across Narathiwat, Pattani and Yala from about 8pm.
A Thai security spokesman said the attacks were believed to have targeted government officials, civilians and infrastructure.
The spokesman said Narathiwat recorded the highest number of incidents with 22, followed by Yala with 18 and Pattani with 11.
"Two people were injured in Narathiwat, while no civilian injuries were recorded in Pattani and Yala.
"In Narathiwat, incidents were reported in Sungai Padi, Sukhirin, Waeng, Rangae, Rueso, Yi-ngo, Lamae, Tak Bai and Sungai Golok, among other areas," the spokesman said.
Pattani recorded incidents in Chanae, Chanae Noi, Cho-airong, Chue-peng, Sungai Padi and Koh Chawi.
In Yala, eight incidents were reported in Yala town, six in Raman and two in Sai Buri.
Security personnel were deployed to the affected areas to secure the locations, assist residents and gather evidence.
Authorities urged residents in affected areas to remain vigilant, avoid locations where incidents had occurred and follow official instructions.
They also advised the public not to approach or touch suspicious objects and to immediately notify the authorities if they encountered suspicious individuals, vehicles or objects.
The situation remains under close monitoring as Thai security agencies step up efforts to restore normalcy following the coordinated attacks.
Security has also been stepped up along the Thai-Malaysian border, particularly in Kelantan, following the incidents.
Meanwhile, a check along the border today showed that Thai authorities had stepped up operations along the border following the attacks.
Cross-border activities along the Golok River were also suspended.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Alibaba proposes US$10bil share placement to fund global AI drive
Article:
HONG KONG: Chinese tech giant Alibaba said on Sunday that it plans to issue HK$80 billion (US$10.2 billion) in new shares in Hong Kong to fund its global artificial intelligence ambitions.
The Hangzhou-based firm has been ploughing tens of billions of dollars into AI, with its shareholders eager to see how it will monetise the huge investments.
"The Equity Placement is being undertaken to extend the Company's global AI leadership," Alibaba said in a statement.
The company intends to use all of the net proceeds to invest in its "full stack AI capabilities, including to expand and enhance its AI infrastructure", it said.
Alibaba on Thursday announced nearly 269 billion yuan (US$40 billion) in revenue in its most recent quarter – a nine percent year-on-year increase – boosted by the global artificial intelligence frenzy driving demand for its products.
The firm is known for its open-source "Qwen" AI models, which have gained popularity with developers worldwide.

Title: Robots can outrun humans, but can they plug in a cable?
Article:
BEIJING: China's humanoid robots have shown they can run quicker than the fastest humans.
Now comes the real test: can they also handle packaging and warehouse operations while reliably performing precision tasks like connecting cables designed to evaluate their ability to work like humans in less flashy jobs?
The five-day World Humanoid Robot Games, which began Saturday in Beijing, combine events modelled on human sports with those designed to test the robots in simulated factories, restaurants, offices and in emergency situations.
The games, heavily promoted in Chinese state media, feature 51 events, including 30 sports competitions and 21 scenario-based contests.
More than 40 per cent require robots to operate fully autonomously, according to Huawei, a tech partner of the games.
On Saturday, two robots ran faster than Usain Bolt's 9.58-second world record in the 100-metre sprint. That was a sharp improvement from 2025, when the winning robot's time was more than 20 seconds. Braking was an issue, as the machines slammed into a thick mat that organisers placed several metres after the finish line.
Another humanoid, the same model as the 100-metre champion, ran 400 metres in 39.7 seconds, faster than South African Wayde van Niekerk's world record of 43.03 seconds.
"The intensity is higher than last year, which places significant demands on the robot's battery management and thermal dissipation capabilities," said spectator and robotics investor Xu Qiaosheng.
"It holds huge significance for the development of China's industrial sector."
Robots will compete in tug-of-war and weightlifting, while Tai Chi and pitch-pot – in which contestants throw arrow-like sticks into a narrow-necked vase – will give traditional Chinese sports a futuristic twist.
BIG TESTS IN SMALL IMPERFECTIONS
Beyond the spectacle, the more revealing tests could come when robots encounter the small imperfections of the physical world: a cable at the wrong angle, an object just out of reach, a shifting package or a missed step.
That tests whether robots can identify objects, accurately position their hands and bodies, apply controlled force and recover from errors without human intervention.
Lumos Robotics chief executive Yu Chao said the games could help improve hardware and provide a showcase for the industry. But Yu said the longer-term value will depend on real-world problem-solving.
"Only when it can work in those end scenarios does it have real value," Yu said. "Simply running and jumping does not improve efficiency."
In addition to more familiar events drawn from human sports, robots will compete in EV charging, restaurant work, emergency incident handling and hand-dexterity contests.
There are also industrial assembly and material loading events. A cable connection challenge is a test of vision, mechanical alignment and force control.
Beijing-based robotics startup Galbot said it would stage an autonomous humanoid tennis match, with robots attempting singles and doubles play, including ball tracking, serving and returning shots.
For Hua Rong, chief marketing officer at robotics firm Zeroth, the real test will come after the demonstrations end.
"The competition will be whether, after the product is sold, it can really solve users' problems," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rubber market to trade higher on strong demand
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian rubber market is expected to trade higher this week, supported by strong demand and concerns over supply constraints.
The Malaysian Rubber Glove Manufacturers Association (Margma) said demand is expected to strengthen, particularly in China, which has pledged additional fiscal policy measures aimed at supporting economic growth.
"Demand for premium and sustainably sourced natural rubber is also expected to strengthen as Malaysian glove manufacturers place greater emphasis on traceability and sustainability under the European Union Deforestation Regulation requirements."
In addition, Margma said El Nino concerns could potentially disrupt rubber production and constrain supply across rubber-producing countries.
Industry expert Denis Low said the Malaysian rubber market is expected to trend slightly higher next week, supported by potential restocking demand from China and firmer crude oil prices.
"Reports of sizeable dry rubber replenishment in China could provide upward momentum if buying volumes are substantial, while higher oil prices may also lend support to natural rubber prices.
"Supply and demand remain relatively balanced, although foreign exchange volatility and adverse weather in major producing regions could influence prices."
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the Malaysian Rubber Board's reference price for Standard Malaysian Rubber 20 added 38 sen to 947.0 sen per kilogramme, while latex in bulk decreased nine sen to 679.5 sen per kilogramme.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PM approves additional RM1mil for Hindu crematorium project in Bagan - PHEB
Article:
BUTTERWORTH: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has approved an additional RM1 million allocation to the Penang State Hindu Endowments Board (PHEB) for the construction of a modern Hindu crematorium in Bagan here,  said PHEB chairman RSN Rayer.
He said the additional allocation brought the total funding for the project to RM2.5 million, up from the RM1.5 million previously approved by Anwar.
He said the original RM1.5 million allocation was found to be insufficient to implement the project, which is much needed by the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Prai.
It will be Penang's second modern electric crematorium, after the facility in Batu Lanchang.
"This additional approval reflects the concern and commitment of the Madani government and the prime minister in ensuring that the needs of Malaysia's multiracial and multireligious communities are given fair attention," he said at a press conference at the project site on Jalan Siram today.
Also present were Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng and Bagan Dalam state assemblyman Kumaran Krishnan.
Meanwhile, Kumaran said the crematorium was important in providing a more organised, suitable and comfortable facility for the Hindu community to perform final rites according to their customs and religious beliefs.
He said the facility would also reduce the reliance of the Hindu community in Seberang Prai on crematorium facilities located farther away.
"This is a long-term facility for the benefit of the Hindu community, particularly in Seberang Prai and the surrounding areas," he said.
Kumaran said the approval of the additional allocation was the result of a joint application and efforts by Lim and Rayer, who had written to Anwar to seek additional funding to ensure that the project could be implemented more comprehensively.
He said the tender process for the construction of the approximately 4,000sqft crematorium had been opened, and the project was expected to be fully completed by the middle of next year.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: CPO futures expected to stay bullish next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Crude palm oil (CPO) futures on Bursa Malaysia Derivatives are expected to trade with a bullish bias next week, supported by persistent weather concerns and Indonesia's B50 biodiesel programme.
CPO futures rallied for five consecutive sessions this week, with the benchmark November 2026 contract closing above RM5,000 per tonne on Friday, reflecting strong upward momentum.
Iceberg X Sdn Bhd proprietary trader David Ng said persistent weather concerns in key palm oil-producing regions could affect production and tighten supplies, lending support to CPO prices in the near term.
"Meanwhile, Indonesia's B50 biodiesel programme is also expected to provide support to the market by increasing domestic consumption of palm oil," he told Bernama.
Indonesia's B50 programme mandates a blend of 50 per cent palm oil-based biodiesel and 50 per cent conventional diesel, potentially increasing palm oil consumption for domestic energy use and reducing supplies available for export.
Ng expects CPO prices to trade between RM4,950 per tonne and RM5,100 per tonne next week.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the September 2026 contract rose RM215 to RM4,791 per tonne, October 2026 gained RM224 to RM4,934 per tonne, and November 2026 added RM211 to RM5,018 per tonne.
The December 2026 contract advanced RM198 to RM5,077 per tonne, January 2027 climbed RM182 to RM5,118 per tonne, and February 2027 increased RM167 to RM5,141 per tonne.
Weekly trading volume rose to 682,863 lots from 582,348 lots in the preceding week, while open interest widened to 342,115 contracts from 327,575 contracts previously.
The physical CPO price for September South increased by RM50 to RM4,770 per tonne.

Title: World Bank projects Lebanon economy to contract by 6.4pct due to war
Article:
BEIRUT: The World Bank on Friday projected that Lebanon's economy would contract by 6.4 percent this year, as the latest Israel-Hezbollah war derailed the country's efforts at recovery.
Lebanon has been dealing with an unprecedented financial crisis since 2019 and was still reeling from the 2024 Israel-Hezbollah war when the Iran-backed group drew it into the Middle East conflict by attacking Israel in March.
Israel responded with a heavy air campaign and ground invasion that Lebanese authorities say have killed more than 4,300 people.
Due to the war, "real gross domestic product (GDP) is projected to contract by 6.4 per cent in 2026, reflecting the collapse in tourism, weaker consumption, disrupted supply chains, heightened insecurity, and prolonged displacement," the World Bank said in a report.
Inflation is also expected to rise to 17.5 per cent this year, according to the report.
The World Bank said Lebanon's economy had strengthened before the latest conflict, with an estimated real GDP growth of 4.2 per cent in 2025, "the fastest since the onset of the 2019 financial crisis."
"Advancing reforms – particularly on banking sector restructuring and fiscal management – will be critical to restoring confidence, protecting stability, and mobilising the financing needed for reconstruction and recovery," Dahlia Khalifa, the World Bank's Middle East director, said.
The international community has been demanding that Lebanese authorities enact financial reforms in order to secure much-needed economic aid.
Last week, parliament passed amendments to a bank resolution law aimed at restructuring troubled banks and addressing the country's banking crisis.
The International Monetary Fund welcomed the law, describing it as "a very good step that reflects Lebanon's commitment to aligning its legislation with the best international practices."
Lebanon has been in discussions with the IMF, which said it would resume its meetings in Beirut next month.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Solehah Yaacob no longer with IIUM after Roman-Malay shipbuilding claim
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM) has clarified that controversial academic Dr Solehah Yaacob is no longer associated with the university after her service ended on April 27.
Solehah had previously drawn attention over a series of controversial historical assertions.
These included claims that ancient Malays could fly and had taught the Chinese "flying kung fu", as well as her theory that the
ancient Romans
learnt shipbuilding techniques from the Malay world.
IIUM's Office for Communication, Advocacy and Promotion for Change (OCAP) said Solehah no longer held a position as a professor or represented the university in any capacity.
"The use of any title or position associated with IIUM is not permitted in any promotional materials, media reports, publications, advertisements, social media content, publicity materials, or other forms of dissemination, whether directly or indirectly," it said in a statement today.
IIUM said the clarification was issued to help avoid any misunderstanding and uphold the integrity and academic standing of the university.
The university did not disclose the reason for ending her service.
Solehah came under scrutiny last year after a video of her saying that the Romans had learnt shipbuilding from the Malays went viral.
She later defended the theory as a research hypothesis based on her study of classical Arabic sources, prompting IIUM to establish an
internal inquiry panel
to examine the claims.
More recently, Solehah suggested in a video posted on her personal TikTok account that ancient Kedah's rich iron deposits could have been linked to a meteor shower or extraterrestrial impact, drawing connections between Gunung Jerai and the ancient iron-smelting complex at Sungai Batu.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Major Japan defence firms stepping up drone development
Article:
TOKYO: Major Japanese defence companies such as Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Ltd. are stepping up their development of drones as the government seeks to make unmanned systems and artificial intelligence a central part of its new defence strategy, Kyodo News reported.
The push reflects a global race to develop drones, whose role in warfare has expanded dramatically since Russia invaded Ukraine.
But their growing use has also raised concerns over civilian casualties and damage to critical infrastructure.
In Japan, partnerships between defence contractors and civilian drone makers have come under scrutiny, putting public acceptance of the industry's shift toward unmanned warfare in question.
Mitsubishi Heavy said in May that it had developed a prototype interceptor drone capable of shooting down incoming attack drones.
"We developed it in just three months through close collaboration between our research and business divisions," Mitsubishi Heavy President Eisaku Ito said.
The company can move to mass production faster than startups by drawing on its existing expertise, including helicopter technology, he said.
The rapid pace of innovation is being fueled in part by data and battlefield experience from actual conflicts.
Mitsubishi Heavy plans to produce a variety of drones in small batches and continually revise their specifications, Ito said.
Kawasaki Heavy Industries Ltd. is working with European aircraft maker Airbus SE on an unmanned aircraft equipped with Kawasaki Heavy's submarine-detection and monitoring system.
The companies are considering pitching the system to the Japan Maritime Self-Defence Force.
Startups, including Tokyo-based Terra Drone Corp., are also racing to develop defence products.
Rakuten Group Inc., meanwhile, has teamed up with a German startup to help the Defence Ministry introduce drones.
The partnership has drawn criticism from mail-order magazine publisher Catalog House Ltd., which said the move conflicted with its corporate philosophy and subsequently pulled its products from Rakuten Ichiba, Rakuten's online marketplace.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: NCT, RHB move to strengthen SME growth ecosystem
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A strong business ecosystem is crucial to supporting Malaysia's small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) as the country advances its industrial transformation.
NCT Group of Companies general manager of sales and marketing Simon Chan said SMEs remained an important engine of Malaysia's economic resilience.
"Facilitating their progress requires a strong business ecosystem, and this is precisely the purpose of our collaboration with RHB Bank and Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP).
"As a developer that works closely with many SMEs, we understand the challenges businesses face as they grow.
"Working with established partners allows us to respond more effectively to these needs and contribute to the continued development of Malaysia's industrial sector and economy," he said.
Chan was speaking in conjunction with NCT Group's partnership with RHB Bank Bhd and Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd to support SME growth through tailored financing solutions and government guarantee schemes.
The collaboration included a seminar series themed "Driving SME Growth with Tailored Financial Solutions & Government Guarantee Schemes".
The seminar provided SMEs with insights into financing facilities, government guarantee schemes, business expansion, sustainability adoption and productivity enhancement.
The series concluded on Aug 19, at Wisma FMM Penang, following its inaugural session on July 21, at Wisma FMM in Bandar Sri Damansara. Beyond financing, the seminars also highlighted industrial development opportunities in their respective regions.
The Kuala Lumpur session featured NCT Smart Industrial Park, Malaysia's first managed industrial park located within the Integrated Development Region in South Selangor, while the Penang session highlighted NCT Innosphere (NIS) in Bukit Kayu Hitam, Kedah, which is positioned to support cross-border trade, logistics and advanced manufacturing within the Northern Corridor Economic Region.

Title: Companies bank on stronger 2H as restructuring drives growth
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Companies are hoping for a stronger second half of the year as they move to turn restructuring efforts, new investments and strategic acquisitions into stronger revenue and profitability.
Robo.ai Inc has outlined commercialisation, technology scaling and supply chain strengthening as key priorities for the second half of 2026, following a series of acquisitions, restructuring exercises and corporate transactions.
The company said its overall direction and strategic moves are now fully synchronised, following a string of completed acquisitions, restructuring exercises and corporate transactions since the beginning of the year.
Robo.ai noted that winding down its legacy operations has cleared away the bulk of its historical obligations, though revenue gains from the newly acquired entities are expected to come in progressively rather than immediately.
"These asset reorganisations and transactions are expected to have a positive impact on the Company's revenue and move shareholders' equity to a positive position," the company shared ahead of tomorrow's financial results announcement.
Robo.ai is scheduled to release its unaudited financial statements for the six-month period ending 30 June 2026.
"The first half of 2026 marked an inflection point in Robo.ai's transformation," said Benjamin Zhai, chief executive officer of Robo.ai.
"We disposed of the legacy business that carried the substantial majority of our historical liabilities, strengthening the company's balance sheet and positioning shareholders' equity to reach a positive position," he said in a statement.
Zhai added that the acquisitions of Neurovia AI, Quantum Core Capital and Alif Holding have brought in cutting-edge technology, seasoned talent and solid operational infrastructure, building a strong base for higher revenue and better profitability moving forward.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dzulkefly: Haze drives sharp rise in asthma, respiratory infections
Article:
KUALA SELANGOR: The Health Ministry has recorded a sharp surge in asthma and upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) cases as haze conditions affect several parts of the country.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said monitoring between epidemiological weeks (EW) 32 and 33 showed asthma cases jumped by 259 per cent, while URTI cases rose by 124 per cent.
Conjunctivitis cases, however, fell by seven per cent over the same period.
"URTI recorded the highest number at 3,674 cases, up from 1,637, while asthma cases reached 219 compared with 61 previously. Conjunctivitis cases dropped to 146 from 157," he said after officiating the Wellness Hub Kuala Selangor and the Prosperous Mind Community Outreach Programme (K-Mindset) here today.
Dzulkefly said seven areas recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today, with five in Sarawak, namely Serian (197), Kuching (185), Sri Aman (178), Samarahan (176) and Sarikei (128). The other affected areas were Sungai Petani, Kedah, and Taiping, Perak, which both recorded an API of 126.
In Kedah, the state Health Department advised the public, particularly residents in Sungai Petani and Alor Setar, to limit outdoor activities due to the haze.
In a Facebook post, the department said Sungai Petani recorded an unhealthy API reading of 149 as of 10am today, while Alor Setar registered a moderate reading of 94.
High-risk groups, including children, the elderly and individuals with heart or respiratory conditions, were urged to exercise greater caution when API levels reach unhealthy levels.
The department also advised the public to reduce strenuous outdoor activities, wear suitable face masks when necessary, drink sufficient water, avoid smoking or smoky environments, and check current API readings before heading outdoors.
Meanwhile, Dzulkefly said 90 heat-related illnesses have been recorded, comprising 71 cases of heat exhaustion, 14 of heatstroke and five of heat cramps.
"Statistics from EW 30 to 32 showed reported cases ranged between two and three weekly. However, the latest statistics up to today recorded nine cases, primarily involving heatstroke," he said.
He said eight of the heatstroke cases involved participants in the Malaysia Games in Selangor, with only one requiring hospitalisation.
"The situation remains under control with close monitoring by the medical task force," he said.
Dzulkefly advised the public to stay vigilant, avoid prolonged sun exposure and seek immediate medical attention if they experience symptoms.

Title: Nearly 1,000 youths light up Kota Baru in Merdeka unity walk
Article:
KOTA BARU: About 1,000 youths, including 20 persons with disabilities, took part in a 3-kilometre walk here last night to celebrate patriotism and unity ahead of National Day.
The inaugural Madani Glow Walk brought together youths from various backgrounds, including students from higher learning institutions, to mark Merdeka.
Kelantan Youth Joint Council information chief Ezzat Hanuzi said the event encouraged community participation while nurturing patriotism through a simple yet meaningful activity.
Participants carried glow sticks and waved the Jalur Gemilang, creating a sea of lights around the city centre.
"This is the first time we are organising the programme, and the response has been very encouraging. Almost 500 participants registered within 10 days," he said.
The walk flag-off took place at the Kota Baru Cultural Centre before participants traversed the city centre.
Ezzat said female participation was also strong, reflecting widespread interest among youths in celebrating National Day together.
He said the walk served as a platform for young people to demonstrate their love for the country.
"We want to show that young people understand the meaning of independence. Walking together with lights and flags creates a lively atmosphere while demonstrating that the Merdeka spirit remains strong," he said.
Ezzat added that the inclusion of deaf and mute participants showed that patriotism transcended age, background and physical ability.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 80-year-old man allegedly attacked with iron rod by neighbour
Article:
audreymd@nst.com.my
GEORGE TOWN: An 80-year-old man suffered serious injuries after he was allegedly assaulted with an iron rod by his 62-year-old neighbour in Jalan Perak here today.
Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report on the incident at 9.55am, following an altercation at 9.30am.
"Initial investigations found that the victim was assaulted by his neighbour with an iron rod in front of the victim's house," he said.
Abdul Rozak said the victim sustained serious injuries to his hands and legs and was receiving treatment at Penang Hospital.
"We have arrested the suspect and seized the iron rod, believed to have been used in the assault at the suspect's house.
"The incident is believed to have stemmed from a misunderstanding between the victim and suspect," he added.
The case is being investigated under Section 326 of the Penal Code for voluntarily causing grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means.
"The suspect will be remanded tomorrow for further investigation," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 167,000 international students contribute RM20bil annually to Malaysia's economy – EMGS
Article:
KUALA NERUS: The presence of about 167,000 international students in Malaysia currently contributes around RM20 billion annually to the country's economy through spending on tuition fees and living expenses, said Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS) chief executive officer (CEO) Novie Tajuddin.
He said based on a study conducted by EMGS, each international student spends an average of about RM10,000 a month throughout their stay in the country.
"With 167,000 international students currently in Malaysia, this has an impact of about RM20 billion annually on the national economy.
"For example, if they study at universities in Terengganu such as Universiti Sultan Zainal Abidin (UniSZA) and Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT), the surrounding communities also benefit from the positive social and economic impact," he said.
He said this at the Malaysian Cultural Discovery Community Immersion programme at Pantai Teluk Ketapang here yesterday.
Elaborating, he said the presence of international students not only benefits higher education institutions but also stimulates local economic activities, including food and service businesses.
Novie said Malaysia is now recognised as one of the world's 14 leading higher education destinations, demonstrating that the country is increasingly becoming a preferred choice among international students pursuing their studies.
"Previously, only four countries, namely the United Kingdom, the United States, Australia and Canada, were often the top choices for international students, but Malaysia is now also on the list.
"This shows that we have become a competitor in global higher education," he said.
Novie said the number of international students in Malaysia had increased by about 23 per cent over the past three years, indicating growing interest among foreign students in pursuing their studies in the country.
He said Malaysia aims to attract 500,000 international students by 2035, as outlined in the 10-year Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint.
"We currently have 167,000 international students. We are undertaking many initiatives to increase the number, and this is just one of them.
"We will go to various parts of the world, covering about seven to eight regions, to promote Malaysian higher education," he said.
Meanwhile, Novie said the five main countries currently contributing international students to Malaysia were China, Indonesia, Bangladesh, India and Pakistan.
He said most international students were postgraduate students, while the overall figure included students enrolled at public higher education institutions (IPTAs) and private higher education institutions (IPTS).
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen drowns, another missing in Sungai Pagalan incident
Article:
KENINGAU: A 16-year-old boy drowned while another remains missing after they went swimming in Sungai Pagalan, near the Pagalan Ferry Jetty in Jalan Bakti Logam.
The body of Jastey Goment was recovered by the Water Rescue Unit (PPDA) at 10.34am today, about 50 metres from where he was last seen.
Keningau Fire and Rescue station chief Senior Assistant Fire Superintendent Severinus Nidzam Sainkui said the second day of the search and rescue (SAR) operation resumed at 9am.
"PPDA divers launched their first dive at 10.30am and located the victim four minutes later," he said in a statement.
He said the body was handed over to the police for further action, while operations continue to locate 13-year-old Khend Romel Ponce Caceres.
The two teenagers were reported missing yesterday afternoon while swimming in the river with several friends.
